question: Which public API endpoints (paths) and request/response models of the Resources module use the word "type" (e.g. ResourceType, resource-types) and which use the word "schema" today? List each name and where it appears.
claim: TYPE (API, Resources module, all require sign-in and list only a 200 response). Paths: POST /resources/types (Create resource type), GET /resources/types (Get resource types, required query param groupId), GET /resources/types/{id} (Get resource type), PUT /resources/types/{id} (Update resource type), DELETE /resources/types/{id} (Delete resource type). Request models: CreateResourceTypeRequest (fields groupId, name, description, propertyDefinitions) on POST /resources/types, and UpdateResourceTypeRequest (fields name, description, propertyDefinitions) on PUT /resources/types/{id}. Field names containing 'type': resourceTypeId in the CreateResourceInstanceRequest body (POST /resources/instances), resourceTypeId in each item of the GET /resources/instances response (row model ResourceInstanceRowDto), and the query parameter resourceTypeId on GET /resources/instances. The operation names (operationId) 'Create/Get/Update/Delete resource type' and 'Get resource types' also use 'type'. Not counted: the field 'dataType' and the model PropertyDataType (a property's data kind, not the resource type) appear in property-definition models and in the instance property-value result. SCHEMA: no Resources API path, request model, response model, field or operation name in the Resources module contains the word 'schema'. In the API description the word 'schema' occurs only as the technical OpenAPI keyword, and in the capability map only as the technical field 'requestSchema' naming the request body model. The word 'schema' does appear in the frontend screens (not the API): the 'schemas' feature has routes 'new' and ':schemaId' (frontend/src/app/features/schemas/schemas.routes.ts), and the 'groups' feature has route ':groupId/schemas' (frontend/src/app/features/groups/groups.routes.ts). These screens' link to the /resources/types API is not visible in the generated files. Instance endpoints /resources/instances and /resources/instances/{id} (GET, PUT, DELETE) use neither word in their paths. The rules behind these endpoints are not visible in the generated artifacts.

evidence.captured_response: "/resources/types/{id}": { "put": { "operationId": "Update resource type" ... UpdateResourceTypeRequest }, "delete": { "operationId": "Delete resource type" }, "get": { "operationId": "Get resource type" } }

CreateResourceInstanceRequest.properties.resourceTypeId {type: string, format: uuid}; ResourceInstanceRowDto.properties.resourceTypeId {type: string, format: uuid}; GET /resources/instances parameters: { "name": "resourceTypeId", "in": "query" }

question: Which frontend screens and routes deal with resource schemas or resource types today, and which word ("schema" or "type") appears in their route paths and screen names?
claim: Three frontend routes deal with resource schemas, and all of them use the word "schema" (never "type"). (1) In the groups feature, the route ':groupId/schemas', which is reached under the 'groups' path. (2) In a separate 'schemas' feature, the route 'new'. (3) In the same 'schemas' feature, the route ':schemaId'. The feature is itself named 'schemas' and its route file is frontend/src/app/features/schemas/schemas.routes.ts. No frontend route path contains the word "type". Two things are not visible in the generated artifacts. First, screen names: every screen's component is recorded only as the placeholder '() =>', so the word used in screen or component names cannot be determined. Second, the URL prefix at which the 'schemas' feature is mounted: the app-level routes list only '', 'dashboard' and 'groups', so the full URL of 'new' and ':schemaId' is not shown. For contrast, the backend API for the same concept uses "type": /resources/types (create and list), and /resources/types/{id} (get, update, delete). Its request bodies are named CreateResourceTypeRequest and UpdateResourceTypeRequest, and the operation names are 'Create resource type', 'Get resource types', 'Update resource type', 'Delete resource type' and 'Get resource type'. So the frontend says "schema" and the backend API says "type" for the same concept. That the two refer to the same concept is an inference from context, not something the artifacts state.

generated/capability-map.json (screens_by_feature.app: paths '', 'dashboard', 'groups' only, lines 435-459; no mount path for the schemas feature)

question: Can a group owner or manager set a time buffer (a break before or after use) on a resource schema or a resource instance today? If yes, on which level, through which endpoint and field, and what is its default?
claim: No time buffer setting is visible today at either level. In the generated artifacts, the resource schema (exposed under the route name 'resource types', /resources/types) and the resource instance (/resources/instances) have no buffer, break, gap, cooldown or turnaround field. A search of all files in generated/ for those terms found no matches. Create/update of a resource schema (POST /resources/types, PUT /resources/types/{id}) accepts only groupId (create only), name, description and propertyDefinitions (each with name, dataType, isRequired). Create/update of a resource instance (POST /resources/instances, PUT /resources/instances/{id}) accepts only resourceTypeId (create only), name, description and propertyValues (propertyDefinitionId, value). Because no such field exists, there is no default value to report. The only way to hold something like a buffer would be a free-form custom property (propertyDefinitions / propertyValues, dataType is an enum 0-2 with no names shown). Nothing in the artifacts shows that any booking or availability logic reads such a property. Not visible here: whether server-side rules outside the request shapes apply any implicit buffer, since handler logic is not in the generated files. The swagger documents only a 200 'OK' response for these routes.

question: What roles can a user have inside a group today (for example owner, manager, member), and which Resources or ManagementGroups endpoints are restricted to which of those roles?
claim: The generated artifacts show only two per-group distinctions: owner and member. There is no manager role and no per-group role list. A group has a single owner (ownerId on GET /management-groups/{id}, isOwner flag on each member in GET /management-groups/{id}/members) and a list of members. Members are added with POST /management-groups/{id}/members (AddGroupMemberRequest) and removed with DELETE /management-groups/{id}/members/{memberId}. No ManagementGroups or Resources endpoint is shown as restricted to a particular group role. Every endpoint is marked only as requiring an authenticated user (requiresAuth true); no role or policy requirement is listed per endpoint. The only per-endpoint hint is that GET /management-groups/{id}/members lists a 403 response, so some access rule exists there, but the artifacts do not say which role or condition triggers it. The other ManagementGroups endpoints (create, update, delete, restore, add and remove member, get one, get list, name-available) list only 200, plus 400 or 404 on some. Whether owner-only or member-only rules are enforced inside those operations is not visible. Resources endpoints (/resources/types*, /resources/instances*) show no role or group restriction. The only 'role' field in the API is a free-text string on the sign-up request (POST users sign-up, SignUpRequest.role), which is a user-level role and not a group role. Its allowed values are not shown.
